t: You're at Leicester Square tube station, on Charing Cross Road, just east of the square itself. It's a short walk from Theatreland, Chinatown and the southern edge of Soho, and the Northern and Piccadilly lines both stop here. Two architects are linked to it. Leslie Green is best known for the first-decade Underground stations in central London, with their oxblood red glazed blocks, semi-circular first-floor windows and patterned tiled interiors. Charles Holden is the man behind many stations of the 1920s and 1930s, and also designed the Underground's headquarters at 55 Broadway.
